# Voice (area `voice`)

Push-to-talk (the app's dictation) and hearing; FERB never speaks (VOICE-409). Most of its code is in the daemon, sense and app areas; its decisions name the files.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **VOICE-400** (owner): Setting up push-to-talk happens in FERB.app; there is no CLI path for it (no `ferb setup --voice`, no `ferb voice`).
- **VOICE-409** (owner): FERB never speaks: no reply, plan line, answer, question or notice is read aloud, for a typed or a dictated message; there is no speech provider and no speech setting. FERB's facts and app guide say it takes typed or dictated messages and always replies in text. Still as before: the one push-to-talk path is the app's dictation (hold right Command + Option, on-device), with an option to send on release; FERB Voice is merged into FERB.app, which answers transcribe, status and request-speech for hearing, with one Speech Recognition grant; FERB's sounds stay.
- **VOICE-410** (agent): FERB.app sends every message without `speak`; `chat.send` ignores a `speak` an older app still sends. ferb/voice/speak.py (Speech, providers) and `voice.said`/`voice.failed` are gone. The config upgrade `no-voice-2026-11-04` drops `[voice] tts`, `voice`, `rate` once, journaled (`config.upgraded`); `[voice] requirement` (hearing) stays. The always-on About line ("Facts about this FERB") and AppGuide's "Talk to FERB" say replies are text only. Send on release stays off by default (`voice.sendOnRelease`).
